close_reason: u8 is a deliberate type choice matching the RFC 5280 §6.1 loop counter semantics. 255 intermediates is far beyond any real PKI depth. No change needed.
description: max_path_len is typed as u8, capping at 255. RFC 5280 pathLenConstraint is an INTEGER with no upper bound specified in the ASN.1. If a cert carries pathLenConstraint=300 (legal per ASN.1), the code compares u8 path_len (which can't hold 300 — the decode itself may fail at the x509-cert layer, or truncate). Also, the policy max_path_len is cast as 'policy.max_path_len as usize' in the check, meaning a policy value of 255 allows 255 intermediates which is effectively unlimited. Using u8 for a security parameter that should be small is fine in practice, but it should be u8 with a comment explaining why (practical max is <<255) so a future contributor doesn't change it to usize 'for correctness' and accidentally allow unlimited path depth.
title: max_path_len u8 type allows silent cap at 255 intermediates
